title: 2:1 Multiplexer
description: Design a synthesizable 2:1 multiplexer.
task: Implement y so that it selects a when sel is 0 and b when sel is 1.

title: Parameterized Counter
description: Build a parameterized synchronous up-counter with reset.
task: Increment count on each rising clock edge. Reset must synchronously clear the count to zero.
constraints: Reset is synchronous and active high.

title: Priority Encoder
description: Design an 8-to-3 priority encoder where bit 7 has the highest priority.
task: Return the index of the highest set input bit and a valid flag.
constraints: Output valid must be 0 when all inputs are 0.

title: Synchronous FIFO
description: Implement a synchronous parameterized FIFO with ready/valid-style enqueue and dequeue controls.
task: Maintain ordering while correctly generating full and empty status.
constraints: Do not read when empty or write when full.

title: Shift Register
description: Design a parameterized synchronous shift register.
task: On each rising edge, shift stored bits toward the MSB and insert din at bit 0.
constraints: Reset is synchronous and active high.
Shift only when shift_en is high.

title: Rising Edge Detector
description: Generate a one-cycle pulse whenever an input signal transitions from 0 to 1.
task: Register the previous input value and assert rise for exactly one cycle on a rising edge.

title: 4-Request Priority Arbiter
description: Build a fixed-priority arbiter for four requesters.
task: Grant exactly one requester, with request 3 having the highest priority and request 0 the lowest.
constraints: Grant must be one-hot or zero.
Highest-numbered requester wins when multiple requests are active.

title: Small Register File
description: Implement a 4-entry register file with one synchronous write port and two asynchronous read ports.
task: Write wdata to waddr on the rising edge when we is asserted. Reads must reflect selected registers combinationally.
examples: write addr=2, data=0x5A → read addr=2 gives 0x5A
constraints: Reset is synchronous and clears all registers.
Do not add a clock to the read path.

title: 8-bit LFSR
description: Implement an 8-bit linear-feedback shift register for pseudo-random sequence generation.
task: Use feedback state[7]^state[5]^state[4]^state[3] and shift left when enabled.
constraints: Hold state when enable is low.
Never allow the state to become zero.

title: Programmable Clock Divider
description: Create a programmable divide-by-N toggle output.
task: Toggle clk_out after DIV rising edges of clk while enabled. Reset drives clk_out low.
examples: DIV=2 → clk_out toggles every second input clock edge
constraints: Reset is synchronous and active high.
Hold the output when enable is low.

title: always_comb vs always_ff
description: Identify the correct procedural blocks for combinational and sequential logic.
task: Rewrite a small RTL fragment using idiomatic SystemVerilog constructs.

title: SystemVerilog Interface
description: Create an interface for a simple ready/valid transaction channel.
task: Define signals and producer/consumer modports so a testbench and DUT can use the same interface cleanly.
examples: producer drives valid/data and observes ready
consumer drives ready and observes valid/data

title: Valid Must Eventually Handshake
description: Write an assertion for a ready/valid interface.
task: Assert that once valid is asserted, it remains asserted until ready is observed.
constraints: Sample on the rising clock edge.
Do not require ready to be high immediately.

title: Reset Clears State
description: Verify that a synchronous reset clears a counter on the next clock edge.
task: Write an assertion connecting reset with the expected zero state.
examples: reset=1 at edge → count=0 after edge
starterCode: assert property (@(posedge clk) reset |=> count == '0);

title: Build a UVM Driver
description: Implement the core run phase of a UVM driver for a simple transaction.
task: Get sequence items, drive their fields onto a virtual interface, and signal completion.

title: Reference Model Scoreboard
description: Create a scoreboard that compares observed DUT output against a reference model.
task: Consume transactions through an analysis implementation and report mismatches clearly.
constraints: Use uvm_analysis_imp or an equivalent analysis connection.

title: Pipeline Data Hazard
description: Analyse a RAW dependency in a five-stage pipeline.
task: Determine whether forwarding resolves the dependency or whether a stall is required.
examples: ADD r1,... followed by SUB using r1 → forwarding may resolve
starterCode: // Draw the pipeline timing for the instruction sequence here.

title: Direct-Mapped Cache Indexing
description: Calculate tag, index and byte offset fields for a direct-mapped cache.
task: Given address width, cache size, line size and associativity, derive each field width.
examples: 32-bit address, 4 KiB cache, 64-byte lines → 6 offset bits
constraints: Show the calculation, not only the final result.

title: UART Transmitter
description: Design an 8-N-1 UART transmitter.
task: Transmit a start bit, eight data bits LSB-first, and a stop bit at a programmable baud tick.

title: SPI Master
description: Implement a basic SPI mode-0 master for byte transfers.
task: Generate SCLK and MOSI and sample MISO on the appropriate clock edge.

title: Button Debouncer
description: Create a synchronous button debouncer suitable for an FPGA.
task: Filter mechanical bouncing and produce a clean single-cycle event.
examples: rapid input toggles → one stable press event

title: Traffic Light FSM
description: Design a finite-state machine controlling a simple traffic light sequence.
task: Cycle through green, yellow and red states with configurable durations.

title: Packed vs Unpacked Arrays
description: Reason about packed and unpacked SystemVerilog array declarations.
task: Explain the memory layout and indexing of logic [7:0] data [3:0], then show how to select one byte and one bit.
constraints: Distinguish packed dimensions from unpacked dimensions.
Include the width of the complete object.

logic [7:0] data [3:0];

title: One-Hot Grant Assertion

constraints: Explain the semantic difference between $onehot and $onehot0.
starterCode: // assert property (@(posedge clk) ... );

title: Stable Data While Stalled

examples: valid=1, ready=0 → data must remain stable

Use an analysis port for publication.
